# Full Stack FastAPI Template

[![Test Docker Compose](../../actions/workflows/test-docker-compose.yml/badge.svg)](../../actions/workflows/test-docker-compose.yml)
[![Test Backend](../../actions/workflows/test-backend.yml/badge.svg)](../../actions/workflows/test-backend.yml)

## Technology Stack and Features

- ⚡ [**FastAPI**](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com) for the Python backend API.
  - 🧰 [SQLModel](https://sqlmodel.tiangolo.com) for the Python SQL database interactions (ORM).
  - 🔍 [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev), used by FastAPI, for the data validation and settings management.
  - 💾 [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org) as the SQL database.
- 🚀 [React](https://react.dev) for the frontend.
  - 🧩 Built into the backend application and served by FastAPI on the same domain as the API.
  - 💃 Using TypeScript, hooks, [Vite](https://vitejs.dev), and other parts of a modern frontend stack.
  - 🎨 [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com) and [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com) for the frontend components.
  - 🤖 An automatically generated frontend client.

narrative.executive_summary: This repository demonstrates strong practices in CI/CD, data management, and testing, with perfect scores in these areas. The security posture is weakened by critical vulnerabilities in dependencies and some partial issues in static analysis and security headers. Container practices are generally good but lack non-root user enforcement and multi-stage builds in one Dockerfile. Documentation is moderate, with some missing architecture documents and low docstring coverage. Performance shows room for improvement, particularly in caching, outbound call handling, and resource limits configuration.

per_metric.text: The CI/CD pipeline is exemplary, scoring a perfect ten with full coverage. It includes multiple workflows that run build, lint, and test steps, all free of actionlint errors. Workflow tokens are restricted to least-privilege permissions, third-party actions are pinned to commit SHAs, deployments are gated, and credentials are securely sourced from secrets or OIDC.

Containerization scores moderately at six and a half with full coverage. Base images are properly pinned, .dockerignore files are present, health checks are defined, and Dockerfiles are free of hadolint errors. However, containers run as root due to missing non-root USER directives in both Dockerfiles, and one Dockerfile lacks a multi-stage build.

Data management is strong with a perfect score and high coverage. Schema changes are managed by migrations, connection settings are loaded from configuration or secret stores, data access is isolated in a dedicated CRUD layer, and multi-step writes use transactions to ensure atomicity.

Documentation is adequate but has notable gaps, scoring six point three with full coverage. The top-level README explains the project purpose and links to backend and frontend docs but lacks concrete setup commands. API documentation is generated automatically, and contributing guides and changelogs are present. However, there are no architecture documents or ADRs, and only a quarter of public functions have docstrings or comments.

Logging is well implemented with a score of eight point six and seventy percent coverage. A logging framework is used, request correlation and trace context are propagated via Sentry with tracing enabled, and a health check endpoint is present. Nonetheless, there is a failure due to the presence of print or console output calls in production code.

Performance scores a moderate five point five with full coverage. Non-blocking IO is used in request paths, list endpoints are paginated, and no N+1 query patterns are detected. However, there is no caching strategy for expensive reads, outbound calls lack explicit timeouts and retries, and resource limits are not configured for any deployments.

Security is a concern with a low score of four and full coverage, capped by critical findings in SEC-02. No secrets are committed to the repository, untrusted input is validated at system boundaries, and automated dependency updates are configured. Database queries are mostly parameterized, and CORS is safely configured. However, there are critical vulnerabilities in dependencies, some medium severity static analysis findings, and missing security headers middleware.

The code structure is excellent with a perfect score and full coverage. There are clear module and layer boundaries separating HTTP route handlers from data access logic. No oversized source files or circular imports exist, function complexity is well controlled, configuration is separated from code using a Settings class, and all dependency manifests are locked.

Testing is robust with a high score of nine point one and full coverage. A comprehensive test suite is present with over a hundred tests across multiple files. Tests are proportionate to source code size, executed in CI pipelines, coverage is measured, and tests contain meaningful assertions verifying HTTP responses and persisted state.
